subject: The reverb's decay as a hidden-line waterfall: twelve frequency slices from bass in front to treble at the back, each a wedge falling away along time.
controls: nave: shape; every slice's tail lengthens along the time axis, 80 px at 0.4 s to 260 px at 12 s.
stone: shape across depth; the treble slices at the back shorten against the bass, to about a fifth of the bass tail on soft stone and nearly equal on hard stone, so the surface's back edge swings.
choir: shape along the tops; low diffusion breaks each wedge into separate echo peaks with notches between, high diffusion fills it into a smooth slope.
doors: position; the whole surface slides away from the bright direct-sound bar at the time origin, 8 to 68 px.
risks: Three controls are shape on the same surface (P3's pitfall); they act on different dimensions (length, back edge, top texture), but at 1:1 nave and stone can be confused.
Twelve slices are twelve outlines and only four mutable paths exist: slices must become stepped node strips or pre-drawn variants, which the sketch ignores.
It's a waterfall plot: the nave itself never appears, so the 'stone nave' character has to come from the header names alone.
Slice spacing is ~9 px on screen; the back third reads as hatching at 1:1.
